title.zh: 卷四 本紀第四: 廢帝
title.raw: 卷四 本紀第四: 廢帝 Volume 4: Emperor Fei

sentences.zh: 陳書卷四

translations.literal: Book of Chen, Volume 4
translations.idiomatic: Book of Chen, Volume 4

sentences.zh: 本紀第四

translations.literal: Basic Annals, Number Four
translations.idiomatic: Annals, Part Four

sentences.zh: 廢帝諱伯宗，字奉業，小字藥王，世祖嫡長子也。

translations.literal: The Deposed Emperor's taboo name was Bozong, style name Fengye, childhood name Yaowang; he was Emperor Wen's legitimate eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: The Deposed Emperor, taboo name Bozong, styled Fengye and in youth called Yaowang, was the legitimate eldest son of Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 梁承聖三年五月庚寅生。

translations.literal: He was born on gengyin day of the fifth month in the third year of Liang's Chengsheng era.
translations.idiomatic: He was born on gengyin day in the fifth month of the third year of Liang's Chengsheng era (554).

sentences.zh: 永定二年二月戊辰，拜臨川王世子。

translations.literal: On wuchen day of the second month in the second year of Yongding, he was appointed heir of the Prince of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongding year 2, on wuchen day of the second month, he was named heir of the Prince of Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 三年，世祖嗣位，八月庚戌，立為皇太子。

translations.literal: In year three Emperor Wen succeeded to the throne; on gengxu day of the eighth month he was established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3, when Emperor Wen took the throne, he was made crown prince on gengxu day of the eighth month.

sentences.zh: [1]自梁室亂離，東宮焚燼，太子居于永福省。

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 1. Since the Liang house fell into chaos and separation, the eastern palace was burned to ashes, and the crown prince dwelt in Yongfu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial footnote marker 1. After the Liang court was torn apart, the eastern palace lay in ashes, and the crown prince lived in Yongfu Province.

sentences.zh: 天康元年四月癸酉，世祖崩，其日，太子即皇帝位于太極前殿，詔曰：「上天降禍，大行皇帝奄棄萬國，攀號靡及，五內崩殞。

translations.literal: On guiyou day of the fourth month in the first year of Tiankang, Emperor Wen died; that same day the crown prince took the throne in the Hall before the Supreme Ultimate and issued an edict: "Heaven has sent down calamity; the late emperor has suddenly abandoned the myriad realms. We cannot reach him with our cries; Our five viscera are shattered.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou day of the fourth month in Tiankang year 1, Emperor Wen died. That same day the crown prince ascended the throne in the hall before the Supreme Ultimate and proclaimed: "Heaven has sent calamity; the late emperor has left the realm. We cannot reach him with our laments; Our inmost being is broken.

sentences.zh: 朕以寡德，嗣膺寶命，掼掼在疚，懼甚綴旒，方賴宰輔匡其不逮。

translations.literal: We, of meager virtue, have succeeded to the precious mandate; night and day in grief We fear greatly for the jade beads of the cap, and just now rely on the chief ministers to correct Our shortcomings.
translations.idiomatic: We, of little merit, have received the sacred charge; day and night in mourning We fear for the realm as for loose cap-strings, and now depend on our ministers to mend what We lack.

sentences.zh: 可大赦天下。

translations.literal: Let there be a general amnesty throughout the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Let there be a general amnesty throughout the realm."

sentences.zh: 」又詔內外文武，各復其職，遠方悉停奔赴。

translations.literal: Another edict ordered all civil and military officials within and without to resume their offices, and all distant regions to cease rushing to court.
translations.idiomatic: A further edict ordered civil and military officers at court and in the provinces to return to their posts, and forbade distant regions to hurry envoys to the capital.

sentences.zh: 五月

translations.literal: Fifth month
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month

translations.literal: (yi)
translations.idiomatic: yi

sentences.zh: [己]卯，[2]尊皇太后曰太皇太后，皇后曰皇太后。

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 2. On jimao day the empress dowager was honored as grand empress dowager, and the empress as empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial footnote marker 2. On jimao day the empress dowager was raised to grand empress dowager and the empress to empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，以驃騎將軍、司空、揚州刺史、新除尚書令安成王頊為驃騎大將軍，進位司徒、錄尚書、都督中外諸軍事。

translations.literal: On gengyin day the Prince of Ancheng, Xu, bearer of the staff, minister of works, inspector of Yangzhou, and newly appointed director of the Masters of Writing, was made Bearer of the Staff, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, advanced to grand mentor, recorder of the Masters of Writing, and area commander over all armies within and without.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin day Xu, Prince of Ancheng—bearer of the staff, minister of works, inspector of Yangzhou, and newly named director of the Masters of Writing—was made grand general of agile cavalry with the staff, promoted to grand mentor and recorder of the Masters of Writing, and given overall command of armies at court and in the field.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，中軍大將軍、開府儀同三司徐度進位司空；

translations.literal: On dingyou day Central Army General, opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes, Xu Du was advanced to minister of works;
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou day Xu Du, central army general and opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes, was promoted to minister of works;

sentences.zh: 鎮南將軍、開府儀同三司、江州刺史章昭達為侍中，進號征南將軍；

translations.literal: Garrisoning South General, opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes, and Inspector of Jiangzhou Zhang Zhaoda became palace attendant and was advanced in title to General Who Campaigns South;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhaoda, garrisoning south general, opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes, and inspector of Jiangzhou, became palace attendant and was promoted to general who campaigns south;

sentences.zh: 鎮東將軍、東揚州刺史始興王伯茂進號征東將軍、開府儀同三司；

translations.literal: Garrisoning East General and Inspector of East Yangzhou, the Prince of Shixing, Bomao, was advanced in title to General Who Campaigns East and opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes;
translations.idiomatic: Bomao, Prince of Shixing, garrisoning east general and inspector of East Yangzhou, was promoted to general who campaigns east with a mansion equal to the three dukes;

sentences.zh: 平北將軍、南徐州刺史鄱陽王伯山進號鎮北將軍；

translations.literal: Pacifying North General and Inspector of South Xuzhou, the Prince of Poyang, Boshan, was advanced in title to General Who Garrisons the North;
translations.idiomatic: Boshan, Prince of Poyang, pacifying north general and inspector of South Xuzhou, was promoted to general who garrisons the north;

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書袁樞為尚書左僕射；

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Yuan Shu became Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu, minister of personnel, became left vice director of the Masters of Writing;

sentences.zh: 雲麾將軍、吳興太守沈欽為尚書右僕射；

translations.literal: Cloud-Banner General and Administrator of Wuxing Shen Qin became Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing;
translations.idiomatic: Shen Qin, cloud-banner general and administrator of Wuxing, became right vice director of the Masters of Writing;

sentences.zh: 新除中領軍吳明徹為領軍將軍；

translations.literal: the newly appointed Central Palace Guard General Wu Mingche became General of the Palace Guards;
translations.idiomatic: Wu Mingche, newly appointed central palace guard general, was made general of the palace guards;

sentences.zh: 新除中護軍沈恪為護軍將軍；

translations.literal: the newly appointed Central Protector General Shen Ke became Protector General;
translations.idiomatic: Shen Ke, newly appointed central protector general, was made protector general;

sentences.zh: [3]平南將軍、湘州刺史華皎進號安南將軍；

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 3. Pacifying South General and Inspector of Xiangzhou Hua Jiao was advanced in title to General Who Pacifies the South;
translations.idiomatic: Editorial footnote marker 3. Hua Jiao, pacifying south general and inspector of Xiangzhou, was promoted to general who pacifies the south;

sentences.zh: 散騎常侍、御史中丞徐陵為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Regular Attendant and Censor-in-Chief Xu Ling became Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ling, regular attendant and censor-in-chief, became minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 六月辛亥，翊右將軍、右光祿大夫王通進號安右將軍。

translations.literal: On xinhai day of the sixth month, Right Assistant General and Right Grand Master of the Palace Wang Tong was advanced in title to General Who Pacifies the Right.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai day of the sixth month Wang Tong, right assistant general and right grand master of the palace, was promoted to general who pacifies the right.

sentences.zh: 秋七月丁酉，[4]立妃王氏為皇后。

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 4. On dingyou day of autumn, the seventh month, Consort Wang was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial footnote marker 4. On dingyou day in the seventh month of autumn, Lady Wang was made empress.

sentences.zh: 冬十月庚申，輿駕奉祠太廟。

translations.literal: On gengshen day of the tenth month, winter, the imperial carriage performed sacrifice at the imperial temple.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen day in the tenth month of winter the emperor offered sacrifice at the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 十一月乙亥，周遣使來弔。

translations.literal: On yihai day of the eleventh month, Zhou sent envoys to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai day of the eleventh month Northern Zhou sent envoys to offer condolences.

sentences.zh: 十二月甲子，高麗國遣使獻方物。

translations.literal: On jiazi day of the twelfth month, Goguryeo sent envoys presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi day of the twelfth month envoys from Goguryeo presented tribute.

sentences.zh: 光大元年春正月癸酉，尚書左僕射袁樞卒。

translations.literal: On guiyou day of the first month, spring, in the first year of Guangda, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yuan Shu died.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou day of the first month in Guangda year 1, Yuan Shu, left vice director of the Masters of Writing, died.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，詔曰：「昔昊天成命，降集寶圖，二后重光，九區咸乂。

translations.literal: On yihai day an edict said: "Of old Heaven completed the mandate and bestowed the precious chart; the two sovereigns shone in succession and the nine regions were all governed.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai day an edict declared: "In antiquity Heaven fulfilled the mandate and granted the sacred chart; two sage rulers succeeded one another and the nine domains were well ruled.

sentences.zh: [5]閔余沖薄，王道未昭，荷茲神器，如涉靈海，庶親賢嵭建，牧伯惟良，天下雍熙，緬同刑措。

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 5. Pity Our youth and thin virtue—the royal way is not yet made clear. Bearing this sacred vessel is like crossing a spiritual sea; We hope worthy kin will assist in building, and the shepherds will be good, that the realm may be harmonious and punishments long set aside.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial footnote marker 5. We are young and slight in virtue; the royal way is not yet plain. To hold the throne is like crossing a treacherous sea. We look to worthy kinsmen and able governors to aid Us, that the realm may flourish and crime fade away.

sentences.zh: 今三元改曆，萬國充庭，清廟無追，具僚斯在，言瞻宁位，觸感崩心。

translations.literal: Now the Three Origins change the calendar and all states fill the court; the pure temple has none to follow, yet all officials stand present. Gazing on the vacant seat, We are touched to heartbreak.
translations.idiomatic: Now the calendar turns and the court is full of envoys; in the ancestral temple there is none to follow, yet every officer is in place. To look on the empty seat breaks Our heart.

sentences.zh: 思播遺恩，[6]俾覃黎獻。

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 6. We wish to spread the late emperor's grace and extend it to the black-haired people.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial footnote marker 6. We mean to spread the late emperor's kindness and let it reach the common people.

sentences.zh: 可大赦天下。

translations.literal: Let there be a general amnesty throughout the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Let there be a general amnesty throughout the realm."

sentences.zh: 改天康二年為光大元年。

translations.literal: The second year of Tiankang was changed to the first year of Guangda.
translations.idiomatic: Tiankang year 2 was renamed Guangda year 1.

sentences.zh: 孝悌力田賜爵一級。

translations.literal: Those filial, brotherly, and diligent in farming were granted one rank of nobility.
translations.idiomatic: Men noted for filial piety, brotherliness, and farming received one step in rank.

sentences.zh: 」己卯，以領軍將軍吳明徹為丹陽尹。

translations.literal: On jimao day General of the Palace Guards Wu Mingche was made Governor of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao day Wu Mingche, general of the palace guards, was made governor of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，輿駕親祠南郊。

translations.literal: On xinmao day the imperial carriage personally sacrificed at the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao day the emperor sacrificed in person at the southern suburb.

sentences.zh: 二月辛亥，宣毅將軍、南豫州刺史余孝頃謀反伏誅。

translations.literal: On xinhai day of the second month, Proclaiming Martial General and Inspector of South Yuzhou Yu Xiaoxiang plotted rebellion and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai day of the second month Yu Xiaoxiang, proclaiming martial general and inspector of South Yuzhou, was executed for plotting rebellion.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，以征東將軍、開府儀同三司、東揚州刺史始興王伯茂為中纫大將軍，[7]開府儀同三司黃法矴為鎮北將軍、南徐州刺史，鎮北將軍、南徐州刺史鄱陽王伯山為鎮東將軍、東揚州刺史。

translations.literal: On guichou day the Prince of Shixing, Bomao, General Who Campaigns East, opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes, and Inspector of East Yangzhou, was made Central Army General; Editorial footnote marker 7. Huang Faqu was made General Who Garrisons the North and Inspector of South Xuzhou; the Prince of Poyang, Boshan, General Who Garrisons the North and Inspector of South Xuzhou, was made General Who Garrisons the East and Inspector of East Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou day Bomao, Prince of Shixing, general who campaigns east, opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes, and inspector of East Yangzhou, was made central army general; Editorial footnote marker 7. Huang Faqu was made general who garrisons the north and inspector of South Xuzhou; Boshan, Prince of Poyang, was shifted to general who garrisons the east and inspector of East Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 三月甲午，以尚書右僕射沈欽為侍中、尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: On jiawu day of the third month, Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Shen Qin became Palace Attendant and Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu day of the third month Shen Qin, right vice director of the Masters of Writing, became palace attendant and left vice director.

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 8.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial footnote marker 8.

sentences.zh: 夏四月乙卯，太白晝見。

translations.literal: On yimao day of the fourth month, summer, Venus appeared in daylight.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao day in the fourth month of summer Venus was seen by day.

sentences.zh: 五月癸巳，以領軍將軍、丹陽尹吳明徹為安南將軍、湘州刺史。

translations.literal: On guisi day of the fifth month, General of the Palace Guards and Governor of Danyang Wu Mingche was made General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi day of the fifth month Wu Mingche, general of the palace guards and governor of Danyang, was made general who pacifies the south and inspector of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 乙未，以鎮右將軍杜稜為領軍將軍。

translations.literal: On yiwei day Garrisoning Right General Du Ling was made General of the Palace Guards.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei day Du Ling, garrisoning right general, was made general of the palace guards.

sentences.zh: 安南將軍、湘州刺史華皎謀反，景申，以中撫大將軍淳于量為使持節、征南大將軍，總率舟師以討之。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Xiangzhou Hua Jiao plotted rebellion; on gengshen day Central Pacifying General Chunyu Liang was made Bearer of the Staff, General Who Campaigns South, and given overall command of the fleet to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Jiao, general who pacifies the south and inspector of Xiangzhou, rebelled; on gengshen day Chunyu Liang, central pacifying general, was sent with the staff as general who campaigns south to command the fleet against him.

sentences.zh: 六月壬寅，以中軍大將軍、司空徐度進號車騎將軍，總督京邑红軍，步道襲湘州。

translations.literal: On renyin day of the sixth month, Central Army General and Minister of Works Xu Du was advanced in title to General of Chariots and Cavalry and given overall command of the capital armies, advancing overland to strike Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin day of the sixth month Xu Du, central army general and minister of works, was promoted to general of chariots and cavalry, placed in overall command of the capital armies, and sent by land against Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 閏月癸巳，以雲麾將軍新安王伯固為丹陽尹。

translations.literal: On guisi day of the intercalary month, Cloud-Banner General the Prince of Xin'an, Bogu, was made Governor of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi day of the intercalary month Bogu, Prince of Xin'an and cloud-banner general, was made governor of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 秋七月戊申，立皇子至澤為皇太子，賜天下為父後者爵一級，王公卿士已下賚帛各有差。

translations.literal: On wushen day of the seventh month, autumn, the imperial son Zhize was established as crown prince; those throughout the realm who were heirs to their fathers were granted one rank of nobility, and dukes, marquises, and officials down received gifts of silk in differing amounts.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen day in the seventh month of autumn the imperial son Zhize was made crown prince; heirs throughout the realm received one step in rank, and princes, nobles, and officials were given silk gifts in varying measure.

sentences.zh: 九月乙巳，詔曰：「逆賊華皎，極惡窮凶，遂樹立蕭巋，謀危社稷。

translations.literal: An edict said: "The rebel Hua Jiao, utterly wicked and utterly cruel, has set up Xiao Kui and plotted against the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "The traitor Hua Jiao, steeped in evil, has enthroned Xiao Kui and menaced the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 棄親即讎，人神憤惋，王師電邁，水陸爭前，梟剪之期，匪朝伊暮。

translations.literal: Casting off kin for the enemy, men and spirits alike are outraged; the royal army advances like lightning by land and water, and the day of decapitation is not far off.
translations.idiomatic: He has abandoned his own house for the foe; heaven and earth are angered. Our armies rush forward by land and sea, and his end is near.

sentences.zh: 其家口在北里尚方，宜從誅戮，用明國憲。

translations.literal: His household in the Northern Ward of the Palace Workshop should be put to death, to make clear the law of the state."
translations.idiomatic: His family held in the Northern Ward of the Palace Workshop are to be executed, that the nation's law may be plain."

sentences.zh: 」景辰，百濟國遣使獻方物。

translations.literal: On jingchen day, Baekje sent envoys presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: On jingchen day envoys from Baekje presented tribute.

sentences.zh: 是月，周將長胡公拓跋定率步騎二萬入郢州，與華皎水陸俱進，都督淳于量、吳明徹等與戰，大破之。

translations.literal: That month Zhou's general the Duke of Chang, Tuoba Ding, led twenty thousand infantry and cavalry into Yingzhou and advanced with Hua Jiao by land and water; Area Commander Chunyu Liang, Wu Mingche, and others gave battle and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: That month Northern Zhou's general Tuoba Ding, Duke of Chang, entered Yingzhou with twenty thousand foot and horse and joined Hua Jiao on land and water; Chunyu Liang, Wu Mingche, and others fought them and won a great victory.

sentences.zh: 皎單舸奔江陵，擒拓跋定，俘獲萬餘人，馬四千餘匹，送京師。

translations.literal: Jiao fled alone in a single boat to Jiangling; Tuoba Ding was captured, and more than ten thousand were taken prisoner, with over four thousand horses, and sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao fled alone by boat to Jiangling; Tuoba Ding was captured, and more than ten thousand prisoners and four thousand horses were sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 冬十月辛巳，赦湘、巴二

translations.literal: On xinsi day of the tenth month, winter, a pardon was granted to Xiang and Ba
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi day in the tenth month of winter a pardon was granted to Xiang and Ba

translations.literal: (jun)
translations.idiomatic: (commandery)

sentences.zh: [州]為皎所詿誤者。

translations.literal: [zhou] for those misled by Jiao.
translations.idiomatic: [province] for those misled by Jiao.

sentences.zh: [9]甲申，輿駕親祠太廟。

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 9. On jiashen day the imperial carriage personally sacrificed at the imperial temple.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial footnote marker 9. On jiashen day the emperor offered sacrifice in person at the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 十一月己未，以護軍將軍沈恪為平西將軍、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: On jiwei day of the eleventh month, Protector General Shen Ke was made General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei day of the eleventh month Shen Ke, protector general, was made general who pacifies the west and inspector of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 甲子，侍中、中權將軍、開府儀同三司、特進、左光祿大夫王沖薨。

translations.literal: On jiazi day Palace Attendant, Central Authority General, opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes, Special Grand Master, and Left Grand Master of the Palace Wang Chong died.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi day Wang Chong, palace attendant, central authority general, opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes, special grand master, and left grand master of the palace, died.

sentences.zh: 十二月庚寅，以兼從事中郎孔英哲為奉聖亭侯，奉孔子祀。

translations.literal: On gengyin day of the twelfth month, Acting Regular Attendant Kong Yingzhe was made Marquis of Fengsheng Pavilion to continue the sacrifices to Confucius.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin day of the twelfth month Kong Yingzhe, acting regular attendant, was made Marquis of Fengsheng Pavilion to maintain the rites to Confucius.

sentences.zh: 二年春正月己亥，侍中、都督中外諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、司徒、錄尚書、揚州刺史安成王頊進位太傅，領司徒，加殊禮，闰履上殿；

translations.literal: On jihai day of the first month, spring, in year two, the Prince of Ancheng, Xu, Bearer of the Staff, Area Commander over all armies within and without, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Grand Mentor, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, and Inspector of Yangzhou, was advanced to Grand Tutor, retained the post of grand mentor, was granted extraordinary honors, and wore shoes in the hall;
translations.idiomatic: On jihai day in the first month of year 2 Xu, Prince of Ancheng—commander of all armies, grand general of agile cavalry with the staff, grand mentor, recorder of the Masters of Writing, and inspector of Yangzhou—was promoted to grand tutor, kept his grand mentor title, received extraordinary honors, and was allowed to wear shoes in the audience hall;

sentences.zh: 侍中、征南將軍、開府儀同三司、江州刺史章昭達進號征南大將軍；

translations.literal: Palace Attendant, General Who Campaigns South, opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes, and Inspector of Jiangzhou Zhang Zhaoda was advanced in title to Grand General Who Campaigns South;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhaoda, palace attendant, general who campaigns south, opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes, and inspector of Jiangzhou, was promoted to grand general who campaigns south;

sentences.zh: 中撫大將軍、新除征南大將軍淳于量為侍中、中軍大將軍、開府儀同三司；

translations.literal: Central Pacifying General and newly appointed General Who Campaigns South Chunyu Liang became Palace Attendant, Central Army General, and opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes;
translations.idiomatic: Chunyu Liang, central pacifying general and newly named general who campaigns south, became palace attendant, central army general, and opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes;

sentences.zh: 安南將軍、湘州刺史吳明徹即本號開府儀同三司，進號鎮南將軍；

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Xiangzhou Wu Mingche, on his present title, became opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes and was advanced in title to General Who Garrisons the South;
translations.idiomatic: Wu Mingche, general who pacifies the south and inspector of Xiangzhou, received a mansion equal to the three dukes on his current rank and was promoted to general who garrisons the south;

sentences.zh: [10]雲麾將軍、郢州刺史程靈洗進號安西將軍。

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 10. Cloud-Banner General and Inspector of Yingzhou Cheng Lingxi was advanced in title to General Who Pacifies the West.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial footnote marker 10. Cheng Lingxi, cloud-banner general and inspector of Yingzhou, was promoted to general who pacifies the west.

sentences.zh: 庚子，詔討華皎軍人死王事者並給棺槥，送還本鄉，仍復其家。

translations.literal: On gengzi day an edict ordered that soldiers who died in the campaign against Hua Jiao all be given coffins and sent back to their native districts, and their households restored.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi day an edict directed that troops who died fighting Hua Jiao receive coffins and be sent home, and their families restored to standing.

sentences.zh: 甲子，罷吳州，以鄱陽郡還屬江州。

translations.literal: On jiazi day Wu Province was abolished and Poyang commandery was returned to Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi day Wu Province was abolished and Poyang commandery was placed back under Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 侍中、司空、車騎將軍徐度薨。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant, Minister of Works, and General of Chariots and Cavalry Xu Du died.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Du, palace attendant, minister of works, and general of chariots and cavalry, died.

sentences.zh: 夏四月辛巳，太白晝見。

translations.literal: On xinsi day of the fourth month, summer, Venus appeared in daylight.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi day in the fourth month of summer Venus was seen by day.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，割東揚州晉安郡為豐州。

translations.literal: On dinghai day Jin'an commandery in East Yangzhou was split off to establish Feng Province.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai day Jin'an commandery in East Yangzhou was detached to form Feng Province.

sentences.zh: 五月景辰，太傅安成王頊獻玉璽一。

translations.literal: On jingchen day of the fifth month, Grand Tutor Xu, Prince of Ancheng, presented one jade seal.
translations.idiomatic: On jingchen day of the fifth month Grand Tutor Xu, Prince of Ancheng, presented a jade seal.

sentences.zh: 六月丁卯，彗星見。

translations.literal: On dingmao day of the sixth month a comet appeared.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao day of the sixth month a comet appeared.

sentences.zh: 秋七月景午，輿駕親祠太廟。

translations.literal: On jingwu day of the seventh month, autumn, the imperial carriage personally sacrificed at the imperial temple.
translations.idiomatic: On jingwu day in the seventh month of autumn the emperor offered sacrifice in person at the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 戊申，新羅國遣使獻方物。

translations.literal: On wushen day Silla sent envoys presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen day envoys from Silla presented tribute.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，立皇弟伯智為永陽王，伯謀為桂陽王。

translations.literal: On renxu day the imperial younger brother Bozhi was established as Prince of Yongyang, and Bomou as Prince of Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu day the emperor's younger brother Bozhi was made Prince of Yongyang and Bomou Prince of Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 九月甲辰，林邑國遣使獻方物。

translations.literal: On jiachen day of the ninth month, Linyi sent envoys presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen day of the ninth month envoys from Linyi presented tribute.

sentences.zh: 景午，狼牙脩國遣使獻方物。

translations.literal: On jingwu day Langyaxiu sent envoys presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: On jingwu day envoys from Langyaxiu presented tribute.

sentences.zh: 以侍中、征南大將軍、開府儀同三司、江州刺史章昭達為中撫大將軍。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant, General Who Campaigns South, opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes, and Inspector of Jiangzhou Zhang Zhaoda was made Central Pacifying General.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhaoda, palace attendant, general who campaigns south, opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes, and inspector of Jiangzhou, was made central pacifying general.

sentences.zh: 戊午，太白晝見。

translations.literal: On wuwu day Venus appeared in daylight.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu day Venus was seen by day.

sentences.zh: 冬十月庚午，輿駕親祠太廟。

translations.literal: On gengwu day of the tenth month, winter, the imperial carriage personally sacrificed at the imperial temple.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu day in the tenth month of winter the emperor offered sacrifice in person at the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 十一月景午，以前平西將軍、荊州刺史沈恪為護軍將軍。

translations.literal: On jingwu day of the eleventh month, the former General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Jingzhou Shen Ke was made Protector General.
translations.idiomatic: On jingwu day of the eleventh month Shen Ke, former general who pacifies the west and inspector of Jingzhou, was made protector general.

sentences.zh: 壬子，以鎮北將軍、開府儀同三司、南徐州刺史黃法矴為鎮西將軍、郢州刺史，新除中軍大將軍、開府儀同三司淳于量為鎮北將軍、南徐州刺史。

translations.literal: On renzi day General Who Garrisons the North, opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes, and Inspector of South Xuzhou Huang Faqu was made General Who Garrisons the West and Inspector of Yingzhou; the newly appointed Central Army General, opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes, Chunyu Liang was made General Who Garrisons the North and Inspector of South Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi day Huang Faqu, general who garrisons the north, opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes, and inspector of South Xuzhou, was made general who garrisons the west and inspector of Yingzhou; Chunyu Liang, newly appointed central army general with a mansion equal to the three dukes, was made general who garrisons the north and inspector of South Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，慈訓太后集戝臣於朝堂，令曰：

translations.literal: On jiayin day Dowager Empress Cixun gathered the ministers in the court hall and issued an order:
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin day Dowager Empress Cixun assembled the ministers in the audience hall and proclaimed:

sentences.zh: 中軍儀同、鎮北儀同、鎮右將軍、護軍將軍、八座卿士：昔梁運季末，[11]海內沸騰，天下蒼生，殆無遺唣。

translations.literal: Central Army with staff equal to the three dukes, Garrisoning North with staff equal to the three dukes, Garrisoning Right General, Protector General, and the eight chief ministers: In the last days of Liang's mandate, Editorial footnote marker 11. the realm seethed; the black-haired people were nearly wiped out.
translations.idiomatic: To the central army commander with staff equal to the three dukes, the garrisoning north commander with equal honors, the garrisoning right general, the protector general, and the eight chief ministers: In the closing years of Liang, Editorial footnote marker 11. the empire boiled over and the common people were all but destroyed.

sentences.zh: 高祖武皇帝撥亂反正，膺圖御籙，重懸三象，還補二儀；

translations.literal: The Founder, Martial Emperor, put down disorder and restored the right, received the chart and held the tally, rehung the three luminaries, and mended the two principles;
translations.idiomatic: The Founder put rebellion down and righted the realm, took the mandate and ruled by the tally, restored heaven's lights, and repaired earth's order;

sentences.zh: 世祖文皇帝克嗣洪基，光宣寶業，惠養中國，綏寧外荒；

translations.literal: Emperor Wen, Literary Emperor, succeeded the great foundation, spread the precious enterprise, nurtured the central lands, and quieted the outer wilds;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen carried on the great foundation, enlarged the royal work, nourished the heartland, and pacified the frontier;

sentences.zh: 並戰戰兢兢，劬勞締構，庶幾鼎運，方隆殷、夏。

translations.literal: both trembled in caution and toiled in founding, hoping that the bronze vessel's fortune might rise like Yin and Xia.
translations.idiomatic: both labored in fear and sweat to build the state, hoping the dynasty might flourish like Yin and Xia.

sentences.zh: 伯宗昔在儲宮，本無令問，及居崇極，遂騁凶淫。

translations.literal: Bozong, when in the eastern palace, had no fair reputation; once he ascended the supreme height, he gave free rein to wickedness and lust.
translations.idiomatic: Bozong had no good name as heir apparent; once he took the throne he abandoned himself to cruelty and debauchery.

sentences.zh: 居處諒闇，固不哀慼，嬪嬙弗隔，就館相仍，豈但衣車所納，是譏宗正，衰絰生子，得誚右師。

translations.literal: Dwelling in the mourning hut, he was by no means sorrowful; he did not keep apart from the inner consorts, and visiting lodges followed one after another—was it only the clothes and carts he admitted, for which the Director of the Imperial Clan reproved him, or children born in deep mourning, for which the Right Mentor was mocked?
translations.idiomatic: In the mourning lodge he showed no grief; he would not stay from the inner consorts, and one visiting bed followed another—not only the garments and carriages he took in, which the director of the imperial clan censured, but children born while he wore mourning, which made a mockery of the right mentor.

sentences.zh: 七百之祚何憑，三千之罪為大。

translations.literal: On what could the seven hundred years of Zhou depend? His three thousand offenses were great indeed.
translations.idiomatic: How could he sustain a reign like Zhou's seven hundred years? His offenses were greater still.

sentences.zh: 且費引金帛，令充椒閫，內府中藏，軍備國儲，未盈硋稔，皆已空竭。

translations.literal: Moreover he squandered gold and silk to fill the pepper chambers; the inner treasury and the arsenals, the stores of the state—before the granaries were full, all were already emptied.
translations.idiomatic: He poured out gold and silk to stock the inner quarters; palace treasuries, armories, and state reserves were drained before the bins were full.

sentences.zh: 太傅親承顧託，鎮守宮闈，遺誥綢繆，義深垣屏，而欑塗未御，翌日無淹，仍遣劉師知、殷不佞等顯言排斥。

translations.literal: The Grand Tutor personally received the entrustment and guarded the palace gates; the late emperor's testament was close-woven in meaning, deep as a rampart wall—yet the ceremonial road was not yet driven, and not even a day passed before he still sent Liu Shizhi, Yin Buxin, and others to speak openly of driving him out.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Tutor had been entrusted in person to guard the palace; the late emperor's will bound him like a wall—yet the emperor never came to him on the first day of mourning, and on the very next day sent Liu Shizhi, Yin Buxin, and others to push him aside.

sentences.zh: 韓子高小豎輕佻，推心委仗，陰謀禍亂，決起蕭牆。

translations.literal: Han Ziga, a petty fellow, was frivolous and rash; the emperor gave him his inmost trust and relied on him, and secret plots for calamity rose within the palace walls.
translations.idiomatic: Han Ziga, a low creature, was light and reckless; the emperor trusted him with his heart, and treason brewed inside the palace.

sentences.zh: 元相雖持，但除君側。

translations.literal: Yuan Xiang though held office, removed only those at the ruler's side.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xiang remained in post, but only to clear rivals from the emperor's side.

sentences.zh: 又以余孝頃密邇京師，便相徵召，殃慝之咎，凶徒自擒，宗社之靈，祅氛是滅。

translations.literal: Moreover, because Yu Xiaoxiang was close to the capital, he was summoned; the penalty of disaster fell on the wicked band themselves, and the numen of the altars destroyed the evil vapors.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yu Xiaoxiang lay near the capital he was called in; the guilty destroyed themselves, and the spirits of the state swept away the foul air.

sentences.zh: 於是密詔華皎，稱兵上流，國祚憂惶，幾移醜類。

translations.literal: Then he secretly ordered Hua Jiao to raise troops upriver; the fate of the dynasty was in peril, and the throne nearly passed to an ugly breed.
translations.idiomatic: Then he secretly instructed Hua Jiao to take up arms on the upper Yangtze; the realm trembled and the throne nearly fell to a usurper's line.

sentences.zh: 乃至要招遠近，叝力巴、湘，支黨縱橫，寇擾黟、歙。

translations.literal: He even called in distant and near, mustered strength in Ba and Xiang, and his partisans ranged abroad, plundering Yi and She.
translations.idiomatic: He even rallied allies far and near, gathered force in Ba and Xiang, and sent his factions to ravage Yi and She.

sentences.zh: 又別队歐陽紇等攻逼衡州，嶺表紛紜，殊淹弦望。

translations.literal: Moreover a separate column under Ouyang He and others pressed Hengzhou; south of the ranges all was turmoil, and the months dragged on.
translations.idiomatic: Another column under Ouyang He and others besieged Hengzhou; the south of the mountains was in turmoil for many months.

sentences.zh: 豈止罪浮於昌邑，非唯聲醜於太和。

translations.literal: His guilt exceeded that of the Prince of Changyi; his infamy was worse than that of Emperor Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: His crimes outdid the deposed Prince of Changyi; his name was fouler than Emperor Taihe's.

sentences.zh: 但賊豎皆亡，祅徒已散，日望懲改，猶加掩抑，而悖禮忘德，情性不悛，樂禍思亂，犷慝無已。

translations.literal: Yet though the wicked leaders were dead and the evil bands scattered, day by day We looked for reform, yet he only concealed it the more; defying ritual and forgetting virtue, his nature would not mend—he delighted in calamity and plotted disorder, savage and stubborn without end.
translations.idiomatic: Though the ringleaders were dead and their gangs broken up, We still waited for him to mend his ways, but he only hid his faults; scorning ritual and virtue, he would not change—he loved trouble and schemed rebellion, fierce and unrepentant.

sentences.zh: 張安國蕞爾凶狡，窮為小盜，仍遣使人蔣裕鉤出上京，即置行臺，分選凶黨。

translations.literal: Zhang Anguo, petty, fierce, and cunning, was reduced to a small bandit, yet still sent his man Jiang Yu to lure men out of the upper capital, set up a mobile headquarters, and choose vicious accomplices.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Anguo, mean, violent, and sly, had shrunk to a petty robber, yet still sent Jiang Yu to draw men from the capital, set up a field headquarters, and pick out hardened criminals.

sentences.zh: 賊皎妻呂，舂徒為戮，納自奚

translations.literal: Jiao's wife Lu, condemned to pounding as punishment, was taken in from the
translations.idiomatic: Jiao's wife Lu, sentenced to labor at the mortar, was received from the

translations.literal: (gong)
translations.idiomatic: (palace)

sentences.zh: [官]，[12]藏諸永巷，使其結引親舊，規圖戕禍。

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 12. offices and hidden in the Everlasting Lane, that she might win over kin and friends and plot deadly harm.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial footnote marker 12. palace offices and hidden in the Everlasting Lane to win over kin and friends and plot murder.

sentences.zh: 盪主侯法喜等，太傅麾下，恆遊府朝，啗以深利，謀興肘腋。

translations.literal: The steward Hou Faxi and others, under the Grand Tutor's command, constantly moved in and out of the princely mansion; fed with deep profit, they plotted trouble at the armpit.
translations.idiomatic: The steward Hou Faxi and others, who served in the Grand Tutor's household and frequented the court, were bought with heavy bribes to strike at close range.

sentences.zh: 適又盪主孫泰等潛相連結，大有交通，兵力殊彊，指期挻亂。

translations.literal: Then again the steward Sun Tai and others secretly linked together, with great traffic between them; their military strength was very strong, and they fixed a date to raise disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Then the steward Sun Tai and others secretly joined them; their traffic was heavy and their forces strong, and they set a day for revolt.

sentences.zh: 皇家有慶，歷數遐長，天誘其衷，同然開發。

translations.literal: The royal house has fortune; its span is far; Heaven guided their hearts, and all alike were exposed.
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty is blessed with long fortune; Heaven moved their hearts, and the plot came to light together.

sentences.zh: 此諸文纹，今以相示，是而可忍，誰則不容？

translations.literal: These documents We now show you—if this can be borne, who could endure it?
translations.idiomatic: We now show you these documents—if this can be tolerated, who could bear it?

sentences.zh: 祖宗基業，將懼傾霣，豈可復肅恭禋祀，臨御兆民？

translations.literal: The ancestral foundation will fear collapse and ruin—how can We again perform the solemn suburban sacrifices and face the myriad people?
translations.idiomatic: The ancestral foundation would totter—how could We still perform the great sacrifices and rule the people?

sentences.zh: 式稽故實，宜在流放，今可特降為臨海郡王，送還藩邸。

translations.literal: Following precedent, he should be sent into exile; now let him be specially demoted to Prince of Linhai and sent back to his princely residence.
translations.idiomatic: By ancient precedent he belongs in exile; let him therefore be demoted to Prince of Linhai and sent to his fief.

sentences.zh: 太傅安成王固天生德，齊聖廣深，二后鍾心，三靈佇眷。

translations.literal: The Grand Tutor, Prince of Ancheng, Xu, by nature possesses virtue; sagely and broad, the two empresses set their hearts on him, and the three spirits look to him in hope.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Xu, Prince of Ancheng, is virtuous by nature, sage and far-reaching; both empresses trust him, and heaven and earth mark him out.

sentences.zh: 自前朝不悆，任總邦家，威惠相宣，刑禮兼設，指揮嘯咊，湘、郢廓清，辟地開疆，荊、益風靡，若太戊之承殷歷，中都之奉漢家，校以功名，曾何髣屉。

translations.literal: Since the previous reign's discontent he has held overall charge of the state; authority and kindness were proclaimed together, punishments and ritual alike established; at his command Xiang and Ying were cleared, and opening territory and expanding borders, Jing and Yi bowed to the wind—like Taiwu continuing Yin, or Zhongdu serving the house of Han; compared for merit and fame, how could the rest even be glimpsed?
translations.idiomatic: Since the last reign's troubles he has governed the realm; power and grace went together, law and ritual alike; at his word Xiang and Ying were pacified, and in opening lands Jing and Yi submitted—like Taiwu carrying on Yin, or Zhongdu upholding Han; beside his merit and fame, who else even comes close?

sentences.zh: 且地彰靈璽，天表長彗，布新除舊，禎祥咸顯。

translations.literal: Moreover the earth revealed a spirit seal and heaven showed a long comet; removing the old and establishing the new, auspicious signs all appeared.
translations.idiomatic: The earth has shown a sacred seal and heaven a long comet; omens of renewal have all appeared.

sentences.zh: 文皇知子之鑒，事甚帝堯，傳弟之懷，又符太伯。

translations.literal: The Literary Emperor knew his son's measure, a matter like Emperor Yao's; his wish to pass the throne to his younger brother also matched Duke Tai of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen knew which son could bear the charge, as Yao did; his wish to pass the throne to his younger brother matched the Duke of Wu.

sentences.zh: 今可還申曩志，崇立賢君，方固宗祧，載貞辰象。

translations.literal: Now his former intent may again be carried out; establish the worthy ruler and exalt the sage lord, that the ancestral temple may be secured and the stars held firm.
translations.idiomatic: Let his former intent now be fulfilled: raise the worthy prince and secure the temple, that the throne and the heavens may stand firm.

sentences.zh: 中外宜依舊典，奉迎輿駕。

translations.literal: Within and without should follow the old statutes and welcome the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Court and command should follow the old rites and welcome the new emperor.

sentences.zh: 未亡人不幸屬此殷憂，不有崇替，容危社稷，何以拜祠高寢，歸祔武園？

translations.literal: We, the unworthy, have unhappily met this deep grief; without this high change, how could the altars of state be kept from peril—how could We bow at the high shrine or return the late emperor to the martial park?
translations.idiomatic: We, the bereaved, have met this heavy sorrow; without this great change the state could not stand—how could We worship at the high shrine or lay the late emperor in the martial tomb?

sentences.zh: 攬筆轶然，兼懷悲慶。

translations.literal: Taking up the brush, Our feelings are torn between grief and joy.
translations.idiomatic: As We set brush to paper, Our heart is torn between sorrow and relief.

sentences.zh: 是日，出居別第。

translations.literal: That day he moved out to a separate residence.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he left the palace for a separate residence.

sentences.zh: 太建二年四月薨，時年十九。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Taijian he died, aged nineteen.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Taijian year 2 he died, aged nineteen.

sentences.zh: 帝仁弱無人君之器，世祖每慮不堪繼業，既居僴嫡，廢立事重，是以依違積載。

translations.literal: The emperor was benevolent and weak and lacked the capacity of a ruler; Emperor Wen always feared he could not sustain the enterprise. As legitimate heir of the principal consort, the matter of deposition was weighty, and so for many years he hesitated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was mild and feeble and lacked a ruler's stature; Emperor Wen long feared he could not bear the burden. As legitimate heir of the chief consort, deposing him was grave, and for years he could not decide.

sentences.zh: 及疾將大漸，召高宗謂曰「吾欲遵太伯之事」，高宗初未達旨，後寤，乃拜伏涕泣，固辭。

translations.literal: When his illness was about to reach its crisis, he summoned Emperor Xuan and said, "I wish to follow the affair of Duke Tai," Emperor Xuan at first did not grasp his meaning; afterward he understood, then bowed prostrate, wept, and firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: As his illness deepened he called Emperor Xuan and said, "I mean to follow the Duke of Wu's example of yielding the throne." At first Emperor Xuan did not understand; when he did, he prostrated himself, wept, and refused.

sentences.zh: 其後宣太后依詔廢帝焉。

translations.literal: Afterward Dowager Empress Xuan carried out the edict and deposed the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Later Dowager Empress Xuan carried out the will and deposed him.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：臨海雖繼體之重，仁厚儒弱，[13]混一是非，不驚得喪，蓋帝摯、漢惠之流也。

translations.literal: The historian says: Though Linhai bore the weight of succession, he was benevolent, mild, and Confucian-weak; Editorial footnote marker 13. blending right and wrong, undisturbed by gain or loss—he was of the sort of Emperor Zhi and Emperor Hui of Han.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Though Linhai held the heir's place, he was gentle, mild, and timid in the Confucian way; Editorial footnote marker 13. he blurred right and wrong and was unmoved by gain or loss—in the line of Emperor Zhi and Emperor Hui of Han.

sentences.zh: 世祖知神器之重，諒難負荷，深鑒堯旨，弗傳寶祚焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen knew the weight of the sacred vessel and that it was hard to bear; deeply discerning Yao's intent, he did not pass on the precious throne.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen knew how heavy the throne was and that this son could not carry it; reading Yao's intent, he did not hand him the mandate.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation notes

sentences.zh: 八月庚戌立為皇太子 按「八月庚戌」

translations.literal: On gengxu day of the eighth month he was established as crown prince—comment: "eighth month, gengxu day"
translations.idiomatic: On "eighth month, gengxu day, established as crown prince"—note:

sentences.zh: 〈世祖紀〉

translations.literal: 〈Annals of Emperor Wen〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Annals of Emperor Wen〉

sentences.zh: 作「九月辛酉」。

translations.literal: reads "ninth month, xinyou day."
translations.idiomatic: reads ninth month, xinyou day.

sentences.zh: 五月

translations.literal: Fifth month
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month

translations.literal: (yi)
translations.idiomatic: yi

sentences.zh: [己]卯 據《南史》改。

translations.literal: [ji] mao—changed according to the History of the Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: [ji] mao—emended per the History of the Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 按是月丁丑朔，無乙卯。

translations.literal: Comment: that month dingchou was the first day of the month; there was no yimao.
translations.idiomatic: Note: that month began on dingchou; yimao does not occur.

sentences.zh: 新除中護軍沈恪為護軍將軍 「恪」原訛「略」，各本不訛，今改正。

translations.literal: the newly appointed Central Protector General Shen Ke was made Protector General—"Ke" was originally corrupted to "Lue"; all editions are not corrupt; now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: On "newly appointed central protector general Shen Ke made protector general": the text originally read Lue for Ke; other editions are correct; emended.

sentences.zh: 按恪本傳，恪於天嘉六年為中護軍，尋遷護軍將軍。

translations.literal: Comment: according to Ke's main biography, in the sixth year of Tianjia he was central protector general and soon moved to protector general.
translations.idiomatic: Ke's biography records that in Tianjia year 6 he was central protector general and shortly after became protector general.

sentences.zh: 秋七月丁酉 「秋七月」三字，原本墨丁，今依《南史·陳廢帝紀》及《通鑑》補。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, dingyou—"Autumn, seventh month," the three characters, were originally ink lacunae; now supplied according to the Basic Annals of the Deposed Emperor in the History of the Southern Dynasties and the Comprehensive Mirror.
translations.idiomatic: On "autumn, seventh month, dingyou": the three characters autumn seventh month were ink lacunae in the original; supplied from the Southern Dynasties annals of the Deposed Emperor and the Comprehensive Mirror.

sentences.zh: 按各本作「秋八月」，訛。

translations.literal: Comment: in all editions it reads "autumn, eighth month"—erroneous.
translations.idiomatic: All editions read autumn eighth month—an error.

sentences.zh: 是年八月乙巳朔，無丁酉。

translations.literal: That year in the eighth month yisi was the first day of the month; there was no dingyou.
translations.idiomatic: That year the eighth month began on yisi; dingyou does not occur.

sentences.zh: 二后重光九區咸乂 「光九」二字原本墨丁，今據各本補。

translations.literal: the two sovereigns shone in succession and the nine regions were all governed—"shone nine" the two characters were originally ink lacunae; now supplied according to all editions.
translations.idiomatic: On "two sovereigns shone in succession and the nine regions were governed": the two characters shone nine were ink lacunae; restored from other editions.

sentences.zh: 思播遺恩 「播」字原本墨丁，據各本補。

translations.literal: spread the late emperor's grace—"spread" the character was originally an ink lacuna; supplied according to all editions.
translations.idiomatic: On "spread the late emperor's grace": spread was an ink lacuna; restored from other editions.

sentences.zh: 以征東將軍開府儀同三司東揚州刺史始興王伯茂為中纫大將軍 「征東將軍」

translations.literal: the Prince of Shixing, Bomao, General Who Campaigns East, opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes, and Inspector of East Yangzhou, was made Central Army General—"General Who Campaigns East"
translations.idiomatic: On "Prince of Shixing Bomao, general who campaigns east, opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes, inspector of East Yangzhou, made central army general"—note on general who campaigns east:

sentences.zh: 〈世祖紀〉

translations.literal: 〈Annals of Emperor Wen〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Annals of Emperor Wen〉

sentences.zh: 天嘉三年作「鎮東將軍」，本傳同。

translations.literal: in the third year of Tianjia reads "General Who Garrisons the East," the same as the main biography.
translations.idiomatic: Tianjia year 3 reads general who garrisons the east, matching his biography.

sentences.zh: 「中纫大將軍」本傳作「中纫將軍」。

translations.literal: "Central Army General" in the main biography reads "Central Commander General."
translations.idiomatic: His biography reads central commander general for central army general.

sentences.zh: 赦湘巴二

translations.literal: Pardon Xiang and Ba
translations.idiomatic: Pardon Xiang and Ba

translations.literal: (jun)
translations.idiomatic: (commandery)

sentences.zh: [州]為皎所詿誤者 據《南史》改。

translations.literal: [zhou] for those misled by Jiao—changed according to the History of the Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: [zhou] for those misled by Jiao—emended per the History of the Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 安南將軍湘州刺史吳明徹即本號開府儀同三司進號鎮南將軍 按

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Xiangzhou Wu Mingche, on his present title, became opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes and was advanced in title to General Who Garrisons the South—comment:
translations.idiomatic: On "Wu Mingche, general who pacifies the south and inspector of Xiangzhou, on his present title made opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes and advanced to general who garrisons the south"—note:

sentences.zh: 〈宣帝紀〉

translations.literal: 〈Annals of Emperor Xuan〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Annals of Emperor Xuan〉

sentences.zh: 太建元年又有「新除安南將軍、開府儀同三司、湘州刺史吳明徹進號鎮南將軍」之文，本傳亦云「太建元年授鎮南將軍」，疑此衍「進號鎮南將軍」六字。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taijian there is again the passage "the newly appointed General Who Pacifies the South, opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes, and Inspector of Xiangzhou Wu Mingche was advanced in title to General Who Garrisons the South"; the main biography also says "in the first year of Taijian he was appointed General Who Garrisons the South"—it is suspected that the six characters "was advanced in title to General Who Garrisons the South" here are intrusive.
translations.idiomatic: Taijian year 1 again has Wu Mingche, newly appointed general who pacifies the south with a mansion equal to the three dukes and inspector of Xiangzhou, promoted to general who garrisons the south; his biography agrees. The six characters promoted to general who garrisons the south here are probably intrusive.

sentences.zh: 昔梁運季末 「運」原訛「道」，各本不訛，今改正。

translations.literal: In the last days of Liang's mandate—"mandate" was originally corrupted to "way"; all editions are not corrupt; now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: On "in the last days of Liang's mandate": the text originally read way for mandate; other editions are correct; emended.

sentences.zh: 納自奚

translations.literal: Taken in from the
translations.idiomatic: Taken in from the

translations.literal: (gong)
translations.idiomatic: (palace)

sentences.zh: [官]「宮」當作「官」，各本並訛，今改。

translations.literal: [offices]—"palace" should read "offices"; all editions alike are in error; now changed.
translations.idiomatic: On [offices]: palace should read offices; all editions err; emended.

sentences.zh: 仁厚儒弱 「儒」各本作「懦」。

translations.literal: benevolent, mild, and Confucian-weak—"Confucian" in all editions reads "cowardly."
translations.idiomatic: On "benevolent, mild, and Confucian-weak": all editions read cowardly for Confucian.

sentences.zh: 按儒有懦弱義，各本作「懦」，疑後人臆改。

translations.literal: Comment: ru has the sense of cowardly weakness; all editions read "cowardly," and it is suspected that later men arbitrarily changed it.
translations.idiomatic: Note: ru can mean timid; the reading cowardly may be original, and Confucian a later change.
